roadmap.goal: Ship slice 09 of ADO Epic #5775 (Story #5796): a re-encryption pass either finishes against the ring it started on or says it did not, and never leaves a credential behind on a key it has stopped naming. The pass reads which key is in force once, to decide what is left to do and to label what it reports, and then loops - while every individual write asks again, because a plaintext is all the port takes. So it holds two opinions about one fact and cannot notice they have diverged. The costly half is the deciding: rows already on the key that was in force were taken off the list before a replacement happened, so the pass never looks at them again, and if the operator's new file dropped that key they are unreadable and unnamed while the administrator is told the rotation finished. The pre-slice spike settled the open design question: widening the port costs six mechanical files, so the clean fix is affordable - and it also showed the two shapes the brief offered are not alternatives, because snapshotting alone leaves the skipped row exactly as unreadable and unnamed as before.
roadmap.overview: Four phases, 4 steps: the port learns to name a key, the pass works against one ring from end to end, a pass that was disturbed says so and walks what it skipped, and the administrator reads it. A fifth phase - the two documentation sentences AC-9.4 asks for - is deliberately absent, held pending the maintainer's call on UI-09-1.

slice_to_phase._held_pending_decision_: AC-9.4, the single-writer sentence in ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/Installation/configuration.md. Held on UI-09-1: ARCHITECTURE.md has no custody section to extend, and the one line that names the epic still says it is not built - which overlaps Story #5781. Whichever reaches that section first owns it.
slice_to_phase._not_in_this_roadmap_: a lock file, lease or advisory lock on the key store, ruled out by the brief; the replica skew after a rotated mounted Secret, which self-heals within one interval; anything about who may start a pass, which is settled and unchanged.

phases.name: The port learns to name a key
phases.description: Encrypting under a key that is not the active one is the thing ICryptoService has never been able to express, and the pass needs it before it can be consistent about anything. The doubles go first: three hand-rolled implementations exist and twenty-nine test files hold a mock, so the blast radius is bounded before the interface moves rather than discovered afterwards.

steps.name: Encrypt under a key that was named
steps.description: RED: a round trip under a retired key - a value encrypted under a key that is on the ring but is not the active one reads back as that key's, is decryptable while the key is on the ring, and stops being readable once it is off. Assert the envelope names the key that was asked for and not the active one. GREEN: extend the three hand-rolled doubles first (FakeCryptoService, RecordingCryptoService in ServiceNowBasicAuthStrategyTest, WriterThatGetsThereFirst in SecretCustodyServiceTests), then add the overload to ICryptoService, implement it in CryptoService with the existing one-argument form delegating to it with the active key, and add the member to DesignTimeCryptoService. The three production call sites keep the form they have. COMMIT: `feat(encryption): let a secret be encrypted under a key that was named`.
steps.scenario_name: Scenario 193 (the half that needs a named key)
red_to_green_tests: A value encrypted under a named retired key names that key, not the active one
It round-trips while that key is on the ring
It is unreadable once that key is off the ring
The one-argument form still writes under the active key
criteria: The doubles are extended before the interface moves - shared-contract rule.
The three production call sites that encrypt under the active key are untouched.
The custody service does not reach for SecretEnvelope.Protect directly. The wire format stays in one place.

phases.name: One ring, from end to end
phases.description: The pass stops asking twice. One snapshot decides what is left to do, what every row is written under, and what the report is labelled with - so the three can no longer disagree with each other, whatever happens to the holder while it runs.

steps.name: Snapshot the ring the pass works against
steps.description: RED: drive a pass over several credentials against a holder replaced mid-walk. Assert every credential the pass moved is under one key, that the key is the one it started on, and that the key the report names is that key. Separately assert the clean path is unchanged - a pass with nothing touching the holder reports exactly what it reports today. GREEN: take the ring once at the top of WalkAsync, build the candidate filter from its active key, pass that key to the new overload for every write, and label the report from it. COMMIT: `fix(encryption): let a pass write every secret under the key it started on`.
red_to_green_tests: Every credential one pass moved is under the same key
That key is the one in force when the pass started
A pass whose ring held still reports what it reports today
criteria: One read of the holder per pass, not one per row.
The clean path gains no work and says nothing new.

phases.name: A pass that was disturbed says so
phases.description: Consistency is not honesty. A pass that ran against one ring while the world moved to another still skipped every row the first filter excluded, and if the new ring dropped that key those rows are gone and unnamed. The pass notices at the end, walks once more against the ring now in force - which turns each skipped row back into a candidate and reads a row on a dropped key as one nobody can read - and says it has to be run again.

steps.name: Notice, walk what was skipped, and say it
steps.description: RED: a pass whose ring is replaced mid-walk by one that no longer carries the key it started on. Assert the credentials the first filter skipped are named as ones nobody can read and are counted as such; that what is reported does not present the move as finished; that it says the ring changed and the pass must be run again; that running it again against a ring that then holds still finishes it and says nothing about a change; that a read-only check reports the same fact and names a key it actually read against; and that nothing said about a ring having changed is key material, in any encoding. GREEN: compare the holder against the snapshot at the end of the walk; when it differs, walk once more against the ring in force and carry the fact on the report. Bound the re-walk at one - a ring that keeps moving reports rather than loops. Correct the service header comment: what is left to do is written on the data itself only while the ring holds still. COMMIT: `fix(encryption): stop a pass reporting a rotation it did not finish`.
red_to_green_tests: Credentials the filter skipped, on a key that has gone, are named as unreadable
The count of unreadable credentials includes them
The report does not present the move as finished
It says the ring changed and the pass must be run again
Running it again against a still ring finishes it and says nothing about a change
A read-only check reports the fact and names a key it read against
Nothing said about a ring having changed is key material, in any encoding
criteria: The re-walk runs at most once per pass.
The new fact is counted off the list beside it, like every other number on the report.
The header comment stops claiming a property the code does not have.
A report that names a key names its identifier and never its material.

phases.name: What the administrator reads
phases.description: The whole slice is about an administrator not being told a rotation finished when it did not, and the place they are told is the panel. A fact that stops at the API is a fact nobody reads.

steps.name: Carry it to the panel
steps.description: RED: extend the encryption panel tests. With the fact present the panel does not show the move as completed, says the keys changed and that it has to be run again; with it absent the panel reads exactly as it does today; and no key material appears in either wording. GREEN: carry the fact through SecretReadabilityReportDto and the frontend model, and render it in EncryptionPanel. COMMIT: `feat(encryption): tell an administrator when a pass was disturbed`.
red_to_green_tests: A disturbed pass is not shown as completed
The panel says the keys changed and that it has to be run again
An undisturbed pass reads exactly as it does today
No key material appears in either wording
criteria: The undisturbed panel is untouched - the common path is not made noisier.
pnpm test, pnpm build and Biome all clean.
